name: Captions (Prerecorded)
explanation: This criterion applies to prerecorded video that has an audio track — for example, a tutorial with narration or a marketing video with dialogue. You must provide synchronized captions for all of that spoken content, and for meaningful non-speech sounds like '[phone ringing]', timed to appear alongside the audio they represent. Captions are different from a transcript. A transcript is a separate block of text read independently of the video, while captions are overlaid on the video itself, in sync with what's happening. This does not apply to video-only content with no audio track — that's covered by a separate criterion.
whoItAffects: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users can't perceive narration, dialogue, or sound effects at all, and captions are their primary way of getting that information while still watching the video. People watching in sound-off environments, like an open office or a train, rely on captions to follow videos without headphones. People who process written language more easily than fast or accented speech, including some users with cognitive or learning disabilities and non-native speakers of the video's language, use captions to reinforce or replace the audio. Anyone in a noisy environment, like a gym or a busy kitchen, benefits from being able to follow a video by reading instead of listening.

codeExample.bad:
<!-- Tutorial video with narrated audio but no captions track -->
<video controls src="install-guide.mp4" width="640" height="360">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
codeExample.good:
<!-- Tutorial video with narrated audio and a synchronized captions track -->
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="install-guide.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="install-guide-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>

howToTest: Find every prerecorded video on the page with spoken dialogue or narration. Play it and look for a captions control in the video player. Check that captions appear on screen in sync with the speech, that they include meaningful non-speech sounds like '[door slams]', and that they're reasonably accurate to what's actually said. It fails if there's no caption control at all, or if the captions are missing chunks of dialogue.

check.question: A company posts a prerecorded onboarding video with a narrator explaining each step out loud. What does SC 1.2.2 require?
choices: Nothing, since the video also has on-screen text callouts
A downloadable transcript linked below the video is sufficient on its own
Synchronized captions covering the narration and any meaningful sounds in the video
A sign-language interpreter overlay in the corner of the video
